title: A solid surface stops another solid from passing through
summary: The normal force is a surface pushing outward, at right angles to itself, so an object cannot sink through.
body: Urone and Hinrichs, in OpenStax Physics dated 26 March 2020, name the normal force as the reason a cup does not sink into a countertop. The counter pushes outward, perpendicular to itself, and that push blocks penetration. Two solids therefore do not occupy one place: the surface refuses the overlap. How large that push is, compared with weight, is a separate sentence on the page and is not this claim.

sources.title: 4.4 Newton's Third Law of Motion
sources.author: Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs
sources.note: Paraphrase only, not a quotation. OpenStax Physics, Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs, published 26 March 2020. The assigned licence for /books/physics/ is CC BY 4.0; the page footer also prints a noncommercial clause, so this card does not copy the sentence. Supports the normal-force sentences: outward, perpendicular, prevents penetration, and matches weight on a flat resting surface.
